verdict.rationale: Buzz's programmatic surface is the documented Nostr protocol. Third-party clients connect directly to buzz-relay via NIP-29/NIP-42, and there is a documented quick start and feature-status table. A separate admin HTTP API (/api/admin/v1) is documented with NIP-98 signed-event auth. However, the protocol extensions are draft NIPs, probes found no OpenAPI or other machine-readable spec, and there is no deprecation policy for the relay API surface. Missing for 10: machine-readable API specification (OpenAPI or similar), stable rather than draft protocol extensions, an API deprecation/stability policy, documented coverage of the general REST surface beyond admin, and independent hands-on corroboration of driving the product via the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Third-party Nostr clients connect directly to `buzz-relay` using NIP-29 and NIP-42 authentication.
Every /api/admin/v1 request must carry a NIP-98 HTTP Auth header containing a signed kind-27235 event.
Buzz is a Nostr relay that speaks NIP-29 (relay-based groups) natively.
